What is your earliest childhood memory?
I was around 2 crawling on the floor in our summer house, then I had to poop. So i just started pooping.

My uncle Bruce.

Nice guy, old, actually my grandmother's uncle.

He would do things like the missing nose, the detaching knuckle, how to balance 12 nails on only 1... All kinds of mind blowing for a 3 year old tricks.

The thing with having a lot of old relatives is they like to dote on you, be super fucking nice, spoil the hell out of you. You as the kid love it, but it makes life for your parents a bit of a pain, cause how can they compete with pizza, pop, cake, and iced cream every time you visit them?

But the biggest thing I remember is being up at his house on the top of a big hill, surrounded by wild cucumbers and poison oak. It was one day after Christmas, I would have been 4. It was a year before school began, that is the only reason I know the year. Uncle Bruce had no kids of his own, gay, but he did have a lot of siblings and they had a lot of kids. So almost every great niece and nephew would get stuff for special occasions. That year he got my brothers and I a set of WWF wrestling toys.

I can still remember the shit eating grin we all wore and how excited we were in the tiny living room after unwrapping it.

1 Jake the Snake, 1 Andre the Giant, 1 Macho Man Randy Savage... And the ring. This must have set the guy back pretty good, because my mother started choking when she saw us tear it open. We played with those until I was fucking 12.

Jake the Snake was always best.

Was a pretty cool post-Christmas Christmas.
My grandfather's legs (I was crawling under the kitchen table). I've been told that I must've been only 18 months.

You weren't crawling and that wasn't all you saw. Thank god you blacked out the rest.

signed, /u/RogerByam's grandpa

I remember being about 5 months old, I was frustrated because I couldn't walk, I didn't like having to be carried everywhere. I could talk though. My mom and my grandma were trying to get my brother, who is a year older than me, to eat with a spoon. He was getting the food all over his head but not in his mouth. Maybe that has something to do with him being left handed, I don't know. I was in another highchair, and I was telling them to give me the spoon. I can do it. But they would not give it to me, they just kept on telling me to be quiet and paid all there attention to a kid who can't even use a spoon. I never used a spoon but I know I can do it. I'm not dumb. They just wouldn't let me. With my brother being a year older than me I thought that I could do everything that he could. except walk. I could talk at his level, Talk in sentences and all, when I was six months old we went to the doctor for a check up, and when the doctor came in the room, i yelled, hey doc, catch the ball. And threw a ball I was holding towards him. He freaked out. He's like how long has that baby been talking like that? I told him, always. Well then they took me in later for a bunch of tests and whatever, I don't remember that. That's about the earliest memories that are interesting.

Sitting somewhere in the house my folks owned, Mom's leg above me, her dress; and the inside of the garage, with the spiders. I was probably about 1-1/2 or 2, given that we moved shortly after, and couldn't have been in that house Also, from the same era, my cocker spaniel. I also remember a green scorpion from when I was about 4 or 5. Weird. Just snippets, but I'm old now, according to current thinking.

I have a vivid recollection from 6 months. I know it sounds like BS but after checking with my parents it can only be explained as being a valid memory. My next recollection is from about 3 1/2 years old.

For those who are interested it's a strong impression of laying in a basket-like container on a wood floor (ship lap) in my sister's room while the sunlight streamed in through the window. At 6 months my father was in the middle building our new house and my mother was there regularly helping out, and bright sunny days are typical of January in the area.
Bouncing on the bed while my mom did laundry, she wouldn't bounce with me. Thus began our long standing hatred on that day when I was about 3.
Two years old: I saw my mother eating, and I went up to her and said "you like to eat too!?!?!?"

Settling in with my parent in their second apartment.I described the place to my mother and she still doesn't believe me.I was 3 years old when they moved out from there. Sadly that place doesn't exist anymore.

Watching our house burn down. I was two, and screaming and crying because I was so afraid of the firemen. They were dressed in their full gear and I didn't understand they were human. They came up to talk to my parents through their mask and their voice was all muffled and scary. I don't remember watching the house burn, just the firemen running around and the shadow of the emergency lights bouncing off buildings. The whole place burned to the ground.
